overview: Despatch (1931): Kwantung's Marine Bureau began government vessel fumigation at Dairen and Port Arthur, with fee schedules and special procedures for US-bound ships, shared with US health and naval authorities.

subfiles.title: Despatch on fumigation service and night quarantine inspection at Dairen and Port Arthur
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the establishment of a government vessel-fumigation service and after-sunset quarantine inspections at Dairen and Port Arthur, together with the applicable fees.
subfiles.summary: Langdon reports Kwantung's Marine Bureau began fumigating vessels at Dairen and Port Arthur in 1931, with fees and special US-bound procedures, asking State to notify US health and naval authorities.

interest: Shows Japanese fee schedules for vessel fumigation at Dairen, with special rules for US-bound ships.
